questions.question: Find the smallest digit x such that the 6-digit number 28x219 is divisible by both 9 and 11.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 9: Sum of digits (2+8+x+2+1+9) = 22 + x must be divisible by 9 → x = 5.

Divisibility by 11: Difference of alternating sums |(2+x+1) − (8+2+9)| = |x + 3 − 19| = |x − 16| must be 0 or 11.

For |x − 16| = 11, the only digit value is x = 5.

Both conditions are satisfied when x = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given number: 28x219

The number must be divisible by both 9 and 11.

Step 1: Check divisibility rule for 9 (Sum of digits).

⇒ Sum = 2 + 8 + x + 2 + 1 + 9 = 22 + x

⇒ For 22 + x to be a multiple of 9, the smallest digit x is 5 (22 + 5 = 27).

Step 2: Check divisibility rule for 11 (Difference of sums of digits at odd and even positions).

⇒ Sum of digits at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th) = 2 + x + 1 = 3 + x

⇒ Sum of digits at even positions (2ⁿd, 4th, 6th) = 8 + 2 + 9 = 19

⇒ Difference = |(3 + x) − 19| = |x − 16|

⇒ For |x − 16| to be divisible by 11, where x is a digit (0 to 9):

⇒ x − 16 = −11 ⇒ x = 5

Step 3: Since x = 5 satisfies both divisibility rules, it is the required digit.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule for 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule for 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits of the number are divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule for 11 Shortcut

Alternatingly add and subtract digits from left to right; if the result is divisible by 11, the number is divisible by 11.

questions.question: {If } X + (1)/(X) = 15, { find the value of } X² + (1)/(X²) .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If X + 1/X = k, then X² + 1/X² = k² − 2.

Given: X + 1/X = 15 (where k = 15).

Required value = 15² − 2

= 225 − 2 = 223

**∴ The correct answer is 223.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: X + 1/X = 15

Formula Used: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (X + 1/X)² = 15²

⇒ X² + (1/X)² + 2 × X × (1/X) = 225

⇒ X² + 1/X² + 2 = 225

⇒ X² + 1/X² = 225 − 2

⇒ X² + 1/X² = 223

**∴ The correct answer is 223.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Subtraction Identity

If X − 1/X = k, then X² + 1/X² = k² + 2.

Cubic Identity

If X + 1/X = k, then X³ + 1/X³ = k³ − 3k.

Fourth Power Identity

If X² + 1/X² = m, then X⁴ + 1/X⁴ = m² − 2.

questions.question: If 33% of 497 = 71% of x, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

33% × 497 = 71% × x

Cancel the percentage sign from both sides: 33 × 497 = 71 × x

Divide 497 by 71 → 497 ÷ 71 = 7

x = 33 × 7 = 231

**∴ The correct answer is 231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

33% of 497 = 71% of x

**Formula Used:**

a% of b = (a ÷ 100) × b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae81406f93295316c397364978d04200122de4783fe01759e9618ae731477b47.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (33 ÷ 100) × 497 = (71 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ 33 × 497 = 71 × x

⇒ 16401 = 71 × x

⇒ x = 16401 ÷ 71

⇒ x = 231

**∴ The correct answer is 231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Commutative Property

The property a% of b = b% of a helps in simplifying calculations. For example, 16% of 50 is easier to calculate as 50% of 16 = 8.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage to a fraction, divide the value by 100. Example: 25% = 25 ÷ 100 = 1/4.

Base Change Rule

If the base increases or decreases, the percentage value changes accordingly. Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base.

Similarly, certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets?

13 - 26 - 30 - 60 ; 9 - 18 - 22 - 44
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:**

**First Number × 2 = Second Number

Second Number + 4 = Third Number

Third Number × 2 = Fourth Number**

For, **13 - 26 - 30 - 60 →**

⇒ 13 × 2 = 26

⇒ 26 + 4 = 30

⇒ 30 × 2 = 60

For, **9 - 18 - 22 - 44 **→

⇒ 9 × 2 = 18

⇒ 18 + 4 = 22

⇒ 22 × 2 = 44

Now, checking the options using the same pattern:

**Option 1) 6 - 12 - 16 - 32**

⇒ 6 × 2 = 12

⇒ 12 + 4 = 16

⇒ 16 × 2 = 32

Option 2) 10 - 20 - 24 - 54

⇒ 10 × 2 = 20

⇒ 20 + 4 = 24

⇒ 24 × 2 = 48 ≠ 54

Option 3) 3 - 6 - 10 - 22

⇒ 3 × 2 = 6

⇒ 6 + 4 = 10

⇒ 10 × 2 = 20 ≠ 22

Option 4) 2 - 4 - 8 - 12

⇒ 2 × 2 = 4

⇒ 4 + 4 = 8

⇒ 8 × 2 = 16 ≠ 12

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at speeds of 39 km/h and 21 km/h. The faster train passes the slower train in 26 seconds. The length of each train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed in same direction = 39 − 21 = 18 km/h

Relative Speed in m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

Total Distance (sum of train lengths) = Speed × Time = 5 × 26 = 130 m

Since lengths are equal, Length of each train = 130 / 2 = 65 m

**∴ The correct answer is 65 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train (u) = 39 km/h

Speed of second train (v) = 21 km/h

Time taken to cross (t) = 26 seconds

Length of each train = L meters

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same direction) = u − v

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04b36750d475332f763eb1260b01c0538be757a63cb252ed0cc085cc290e5daf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance to be covered = L + L = 2L

⇒ Relative Speed = (39 − 21) × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 2L = 5 × 26

⇒ 2L = 130

⇒ L = 130 / 2

⇒ L = 65 meters

**∴ The correct answer is 65 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Distance

When one train crosses another train (stationary or moving), the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of both trains (L₁ + L₂).

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 3 years. In how many years will it amount to 9 times of itself?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Compound Interest, if a sum becomes n times in t years, it becomes nk times in (k × t) years.

Given: Sum triples (n = 3) in t = 3 years.

Target: Sum becomes 9 times, which is 3² (so, k = 2).

Required time = k × t = 2 × 3 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Sum (P) triples itself in 3 years at compound interest.

Formula used: A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52a3104787f0eafee814a608aed899e55c4762496730544a2e48fdedafc70f5e.png] 

⇒ Case 1: 3P = P(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)³ --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: 9P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 9 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 3² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ Substituting value of 3 from Eq. 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)³]² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)³ × ² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁶ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ By comparing powers, t = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A after n years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where P is principal and r is the annual interest rate.

CI vs SI Growth

Simple Interest (SI) grows linearly with time, whereas Compound Interest (CI) grows geometrically (exponentially) over time.

Difference for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula: Difference = P × (r/100)².

questions.question: The cost price of 28 mangoes is the same as the selling price of 25 mangoes. Find the profit percentage.

Profit % = (3 / 25) × 100

Profit % = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

**Given:**

questions.question: Under the Right to Equality, of the Indian Constitution, which type of equality is ensured in public employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equality of opportunity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16** of the **Constitution of India** provides for **equality of opportunity** for all **citizens** in matters relating to **employment** or **appointment** to any office under the **State**.
 
• It ensures that no **citizen** shall, on grounds only of **religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence** or any of them, be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any **employment** or office under the **State**.
 
• This provision is a cornerstone of the **Right to Equality**, which is one of the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed under **Part III** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure that the **State** acts as a model employer and provides a **level playing field** to all **eligible citizens** regardless of their background.
 
• While it mandates **equality of opportunity**, it does not prevent the **State** from laying down necessary **qualifications** (educational or technical) for recruitment to **government services**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Equality (Articles 14–18):**

 
 
• **Article 14**: Guarantees **equality before the law** and **equal protection of the laws** within the territory of **India**.
 
• **Article 15**: Prohibits **discrimination** on grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth** in access to public places.
 
• **Article 17**: Mandates the **abolition of untouchability** and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18**: Relates to the **abolition of titles**, except military and academic distinctions, to ensure social equality.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Political Equality:**
 
 
• While **Political equality** is reflected through **Universal Adult Suffrage** (**Article 326**), and **Economic equality** is a goal mentioned in the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (**Part IV**), **Article 16** specifically focuses on **procedural equality** in the **job market** controlled by the **government**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exceptions to Article 16:**

 
 
• **Article 16(3)**: **Parliament** can make laws prescribing **residence** as a condition for certain **employment** within a **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
• **Article 16(4)**: Allows the **State** to make provisions for the **reservation** of appointments or posts in favor of any **backward class** of citizens which, in the opinion of the **State**, is not adequately represented in the services.
 
• **103rd Amendment Act, 2019**: Introduced **Article 16(6)**, which permits the **State** to provide up to **10% reservation** for the **Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** in **public employment**.
 
• **Article 16(5)**: Provides that a law can require that the incumbent of an office in connection with the affairs of any **religious or denominational institution** shall belong to a particular **religion**.

questions.question: Two alloys are made by mixing metals A and B in the ratio 3 : 2 and 5 : 3, respectively. Equal quantities of the two alloys are melted and mixed together. Find the ratio of metals A and B in the final mixture.

Alloy 2 → (5 : 3) × 5 = 25 : 15

⇒ Metal A in Alloy 2 = (5/8) × 40 = 25 units

⇒ Metal B in Alloy 2 = (3/8) × 40 = 15 units

⇒ Total Metal A in final mixture = 24 + 25 = 49 units

⇒ Total Metal B in final mixture = 16 + 15 = 31 units

⇒ Final Ratio A : B = 49 : 31

**∴ The correct answer is 49 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Cross Rule

The ratio of the weights of the two mixtures is inversely proportional to the difference between their individual concentration and the mean concentration.

questions.question: A body of mass 4 kg has a kinetic energy of 72 J. Its speed is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 m/s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kinetic Energy (KE)** of an object is the energy it possesses due to its **motion**. It is mathematically defined by the formula:

 Kinetic Energy (KE) = (1)/(2)mv² 

 Where **m** is the **mass** of the body and **v** is its **speed** or **velocity**.
 
• Given data in the question:

 **Mass (m)** = 4 kg

 **Kinetic Energy (KE)** = 72 J
 
• To find the **speed (v)**, we rearrange the formula:

 v² = (2 times KE)/(m) 

 v = sqrt{(2 times KE)/(m)} 
 
• Substituting the values:

 v = sqrt{(2 times 72)/(4)} 

 v = sqrt{(144)/(4)} 

 v = sqrt{36} 

 **v = 6 m/s**
 
• The other options are incorrect because:

 If v = 4 m/s, KE = 1/2 × 4 × 16 = 32 J.

 If v = 9 m/s, KE = 1/2 × 4 × 81 = 162 J.

 If v = 3 m/s, KE = 1/2 × 4 × 9 = 18 J.

 Only a speed of **6 m/s** satisfies the given energy of 72 J.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction.
 
• The **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to 1 kg·m²/s².
 
• Kinetic energy is directly proportional to the **mass** of the object and to the **square of its velocity**. This means if the speed of an object doubles, its kinetic energy increases fourfold.
 
• The relationship between **Kinetic Energy (K)** and **Linear Momentum (p)** is given by the formula:

 K = frac{p²}{2m}

questions.question: Transportation of water in plants takes place through ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized vascular tissue in plants that acts as the primary channel for the **transportation of water** and dissolved minerals from the roots to the stems and leaves.
 
• The movement of water in the xylem is **unidirectional**, meaning it only moves upwards from the soil to the upper parts of the plant.
 
• **Phloem** is another vascular tissue responsible for the **translocation of food** (nutrients/sugars) prepared in the leaves to all other parts of the plant. Its movement is **bidirectional**.
 
• **Parenchyma** is a simple permanent tissue that makes up the bulk of the plant body; its main functions are **storage of food**, photosynthesis, and providing buoyancy to aquatic plants (aerenchyma).
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a tissue composed of dead cells with thick lignified walls, providing **mechanical strength** and structural support to the plant parts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Xylem is composed of four distinct types of elements: **Tracheids**, **Vessels**, **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibres**. Among these, xylem parenchyma is the only living component.
 
• The transport of water through the xylem is driven by two main mechanisms: **Root Pressure** (at night or in low transpiration conditions) and **Transpiration Pull** (the suction force created by the evaporation of water from leaf surfaces).
 
• The **Vascular Bundle** in plants is the collective term for the arrangement of xylem and phloem together.
 
• In woody plants, the **secondary xylem** forms what we commonly refer to as **wood**.

questions.question: The circumference of two circles are in the ratio 5:9 . Calculate the ratio of their areas.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Circumferences (C₁ : C₂) = Ratio of Radii (r₁ : r₂) = 5 : 9

Ratio of Areas (A₁ : A₂) = (Ratio of Radii)²

⇒ Ratio of Areas = 5² : 9² = 25 : 81

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of circumferences of two circles = 5 : 9

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle (C) = 2 × π × r

Area of a circle (A) = π × r²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3faa46ea5a557b09845f07116288a0260526d53f4444cd546fd988cc464fb810.png] 

Let the radii of the two circles be r₁ and r₂ respectively.

⇒ C₁ / C₂ = (2 × π × r₁) / (2 × π × r₂) = 5 / 9

⇒ r₁ / r₂ = 5 / 9

Ratio of their areas (A₁ : A₂):

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (π × r₁²) / (π × r₂²)

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (r₁ / r₂)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (5 / 9)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 25 / 81

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Circles

Since all circles are similar, the ratio of any linear dimension (radius, diameter, circumference) is always equal. Let the ratio of radii be x : y, then the ratio of areas is always x² : y².

Area of Sector

Area of a sector with central angle θ is given by (θ/360) × πr².

Length of Arc

Length of an arc subtending angle θ at the center is (θ/360) × 2πr.

questions.question: In a division sum, the divisor is 10 times the quotient and 6 times the remainder. If the remainder is 25, what is the dividend?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisor = 6 × Remainder = 6 × 25 = 150

Quotient = Divisor ÷ 10 = 150 ÷ 10 = 15

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

Dividend = (150 × 15) + 25

Dividend = 2250 + 25 = 2275

**∴ The correct answer is 2275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Remainder (R) = 25

Divisor (D) = 10 × Quotient (Q)

Divisor (D) = 6 × Remainder (R)

**Formula Used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b03eef461dc889d7864b11a2aa01414a80737efe7b00a215a62833e95d74c062.png] 

⇒ Divisor = 6 × 25 = 150

⇒ 10 × Quotient = 150

⇒ Quotient = 150 ÷ 10 = 15

⇒ Dividend = (150 × 15) + 25

⇒ Dividend = 2250 + 25

⇒ Dividend = 2275

**∴ The correct answer is 2275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division Algorithm

The fundamental relation in division is Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder.

Remainder Property

The remainder obtained in any division sum is always non-negative and strictly less than the divisor (0 ≤ R < D).

Verification Rule

To verify a division sum, multiply the divisor by the quotient and add the remainder; the result must equal the dividend.

questions.question: 4% of a number is what percentage of 16% of the same number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both percentages are calculated on the same number, the number effectively cancels out.

Required % = (Value 1 ÷ Value 2) × 100

⇒ (4 ÷ 16) × 100

⇒ (1/4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

First value = 4% of a number

Second value = 16% of the same number

Formula used: Percentage = (Part / Total) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/83030a87a9367e60d3c73dcced08a1b67ed334648d5aadcdcad909233c264ab6.png] 

Let the number be x.

⇒ First value = (4/100) × x = 0.04x

⇒ Second value = (16/100) × x = 0.16x

⇒ Required % = (0.04x / 0.16x) × 100

⇒ Required % = (4 / 16) × 100

⇒ Required % = 1/4 × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Rule

In any "A is what percent of B" question, the term following 'of' is always the denominator (base). Required % = (A/B) × 100.

Fraction to Percentage

To convert any fraction x/y into a percentage, multiply by 100. Common values: 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, 3/4 = 75%.

Percentage Change

Percentage increase or decrease is calculated as (Difference / Original Value) × 100.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes a double concave lens?

options.text: It is equally thick at the center and edges; it neither converges nor diverges light.
It is thinner at the edges and thicker in the middle; it converges light rays.
It is thicker at the edges and thinner in the middle; it diverges light rays.
It is used to focus light to a single point.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is thicker at the edges and thinner in the middle; it diverges light rays.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **double concave lens** is a lens that has two inward-curving surfaces. Because of its shape, it is **thicker at the periphery (edges)** and **thinner at the center**.
 
• This type of lens is classified as a **diverging lens** because it causes parallel rays of light passing through it to **spread out** (diverge).
 
• When parallel light rays enter a concave lens, they are refracted away from the **principal axis**. When these diverged rays are produced backwards, they appear to meet at a single point called the **principal focus**.
 
• The option describing a lens that is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges refers to a **convex lens** (converging lens), which brings light rays to a focus.
 
• A lens that is equally thick at the center and edges (like a rectangular **glass slab**) does not cause a net convergence or divergence of light rays, although it may cause a lateral shift.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia Correction:** Concave lenses are used in eyeglasses to correct **nearsightedness (myopia)**, helping to focus the image correctly onto the retina.
 
• **Image Formation:** A concave lens always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image of an object, regardless of the distance between the object and the lens.
 
• **Focal Length:** Following the Cartesian sign convention, the **focal length** of a concave lens is always taken as **negative**.
 
• **Optical Instruments:** These lenses are used in combination with other lenses in **telescopes**, **binoculars**, and **cameras** to improve image quality and reduce aberrations. They are also used in **door peepholes** to provide a wide-angle view.

Total Amount (A)

questions.question: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 84 instead of 100. Due to this, the avarage marks of the class got decreased by (8)/(7) . What is the number of students in the class?

questions.question: During the chlor-alkali process, which of the following statements is correct regarding the products formed at different electrodes?

options.text: Sodium hydroxide is formed at the anode and chlorine gas at the cathode.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen gas is released at the cathode and chlorine gas at the anode.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chlor-alkali process** is an industrial method for the **electrolysis** of a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride, commonly known as **brine**.
 
• During this process, electricity is passed through the brine solution, causing it to decompose into three main products: **Chlorine gas**, **Hydrogen gas**, and **Sodium hydroxide**.
 
• **At the Anode (Positive Electrode):** Negatively charged chloride ions (Cl-) are attracted to the anode, where they lose electrons (oxidation) to form **Chlorine gas (Cl2)**. The reaction is: 2Cl⁻ (aq) rightarrow Cl₂ (g) + 2e⁻ .
 
• **At the Cathode (Negative Electrode):** Positively charged hydrogen ions (from the dissociation of water) are attracted to the cathode, where they gain electrons (reduction) to form **Hydrogen gas (H2)**. The reaction is: 2H₂O (l) + 2e⁻ rightarrow H₂ (g) + 2OH⁻ (aq) .
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH):** The remaining sodium ions (Na+) and the hydroxide ions (OH-) formed at the cathode combine to produce **Sodium hydroxide** in the solution near the cathode.
 
• Therefore, the statements in options 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect because they misidentify the location or the nature of the products formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The name **Chlor-alkali** is derived from the products: **Chlor** for chlorine and **alkali** for sodium hydroxide (an alkaline substance).
 
• **Chlorine gas** is used in water treatment, manufacturing **PVC**, disinfectants, and pesticides.
 
• **Hydrogen gas** is used as a **fuel**, for making margarine (hydrogenation), and in the production of **ammonia** for fertilizers.
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** is vital in the manufacturing of **soaps and detergents**, paper making, and de-greasing metals.
 
• The overall chemical equation for the process is: 2NaCl (aq) + 2H₂O (l) rightarrow 2NaOH (aq) + Cl₂ (g) + H₂ (g) .

questions.question: Which of the following is a mechanical method of weed control?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hand weeding**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical weed control** refers to the use of **physical force** or **tools** to remove or destroy weeds. **Hand weeding** is one of the oldest and most effective mechanical methods, where weeds are pulled out by hand or removed using small hand tools.
 
• **Spraying herbicides** is classified as a **chemical method** of weed control. It involves the use of synthetic chemicals to inhibit the growth of or kill unwanted plants.
 
• **Crop rotation** is a **cultural method** of weed control. By changing the types of crops grown in a specific field over different seasons, the growth cycle of weeds specific to a particular crop is disrupted.
 
• **Seed treatment** is generally a **preventive measure** or a method to control **seed-borne diseases** and **pests**. While using clean seeds prevents the introduction of weeds, it is not a direct mechanical method for controlling existing weeds in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other common **mechanical methods** include **tillage** (ploughing the soil), **hoeing**, **digging**, **mowing** (cutting weeds to ground level), and **mulching** (covering soil to block sunlight).
 
• **Mechanical methods** are preferred in **organic farming** because they do not leave **chemical residues** in the soil or food products and are generally **environmentally friendly**.
 
• **Biological weed control** involves using living organisms like **insects**, **fungi**, or **bacteria** that specifically target and destroy weed species without harming the main crop.
 
• The **Critical Period of Weed Competition** is the stage in a crop's life cycle when weed interference causes the most significant **yield loss**; mechanical weeding is most effective during this time.

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 4 kHz and a wavelength of 25 cm. How much time will it take to travel a distance of 2.5 km?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5 s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the **speed (v)**, **frequency (f)**, and **wavelength (λ)** of a wave is defined by the formula: v = f times lambda .
 
• To solve the problem, we first convert all given values into **SI units**:
 
 
• **Frequency (f)**: 4 kHz = 4000 Hz (since 1 kHz = 1000 Hz).
 
• **Wavelength (λ)**: 25 cm = 0.25 m (since 1 m = 100 cm).
 
• **Distance (d)**: 2.5 km = 2500 m (since 1 km = 1000 m).
 
 
 
• Calculate the **speed of the sound wave**:
 
 
• Speed (v) = 4000 Hz × 0.25 m = **1000 m/s**.
 
 
 
• The **time (t)** taken to travel a specific **distance (d)** at a constant **speed (v)** is calculated using the formula: Time = Distance / Speed.
 
• Calculate the **total time**:
 
 
• t = 2500 m / 1000 m/s = **2.5 s**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the sound wave takes exactly **2.5 seconds** to travel the distance of **2.5 km**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sound waves** are mechanical **longitudinal waves** that require a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel.
 
• The **speed of sound** varies depending on the **medium**; it is generally fastest in solids and slowest in gases.
 
• The **audible range** of sound for a healthy human ear is typically between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the number of vibrations or cycles per unit of time, and its unit is **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• **Wavelength** is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions in a sound wave.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **proton** is a fundamental subatomic particle found in the **nucleus** of every atom.
 
• It carries a **positive electric charge**, which is equal in magnitude but opposite in sign to the charge of an electron.
 
• The **mass** of a proton is approximately 1.6726 x 10⁻²⁷ kg. In comparison to an **electron**, a proton is about **1836 times** heavier. In basic physics and chemistry textbooks, this value is often approximated as **2000 times** for ease of comparison.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because a particle with no charge in the nucleus is a **neutron**.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because the mass of an electron is negligible (about 1/1836) compared to a proton.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because **electrons** are negatively charged, while protons are **positively charged**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The number of protons in the nucleus is known as the **atomic number** (denoted by the symbol **Z**), which determines the chemical identity of the element.
 
• Protons are not fundamental particles; they are composed of even smaller particles called **quarks**. Specifically, a proton consists of two **up quarks** and one **down quark**.
 
• The mass of a proton is 1.6726 times 10⁻²⁷ kg, whereas the mass of an electron is 9.109 times 10⁻³¹ kg.

questions.question: Waste products formed in body by energy generation processes are desirable to remove by which of the following life processes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Excretion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Excretion** is the biological process involved in the removal of harmful **metabolic wastes** from the body that are generated during various chemical reactions.
 
• During **energy generation** processes like **cellular respiration**, the body produces various by-products such as **carbon dioxide**, water, and **nitrogenous wastes** (like urea or uric acid).
 
• These waste products are toxic to the organism if they accumulate; therefore, their removal is essential for maintaining **homeostasis**.
 
• **Circulation** is the process of transporting oxygen, nutrients, and waste products through the body via blood, but it is not the process of removal itself.
 
• **Digestion** refers to the mechanical and chemical breakdown of food into smaller components, while **Nutrition** is the overall process of obtaining and utilizing food for growth and repair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In human beings, the primary organs of **Excretion** are the **Kidneys**, which filter the blood to produce **urine**.
 
• The **Lungs** are responsible for the excretion of gaseous waste, specifically **carbon dioxide**, which is a byproduct of respiration.
 
• The **Skin** also plays a minor role in excretion by removing excess salts, urea, and water through **sweat glands**.
 
• In plants, waste products are removed through different mechanisms such as **transpiration** (for excess water), storage in cellular **vacuoles**, or by shedding old leaves and bark.
 
• It is important to distinguish between **Excretion** (removal of metabolic waste) and **Egestion** (removal of undigested food from the gut).

• The centre follows the **FAIR** principles—**Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable**—to ensure data quality and utility for global and national research.
 
 
 
• **Genome India Project (GIP):**
 
 
• Launched in **2020**, the project involved a collaboration of **20 premier institutions**, including the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** in **Bengaluru** and several **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)**.
 
• Its primary goal was to catalog **genetic variations** among the diverse **ethnic groups** of **India**, which comprises over **4,600** distinct population groups.
 
• The project helps in identifying **biomarkers** for diseases like **Type 2 Diabetes**, **Cardiovascular diseases**, and rare **genetic disorders**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Local Storage:**
 
 
• Storing genomic data within **India** at the **IBDC** is a strategic move for **data sovereignty** and **national security**, preventing the unauthorized exploitation of **Indian genetic resources** by foreign entities.
 
• It facilitates the development of indigenous **diagnostic kits** and **vaccines** by providing a baseline of the **Indian reference genome**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data Accessibility:** While the data is stored at **IBDC**, access is regulated through a **Data Access Committee (DAC)** to ensure ethical usage and **privacy protection** of the donors.
 
• **Inclusion of Diversity:** The **2025** dataset includes samples from **tribal populations** and **isolated communities**, making it one of the most genetically diverse **biographical archives** in the world.
 
• **Future Scope:** The **Department of Biotechnology** plans to expand the repository to include **phenotypic data** (physical traits) along with **genotypic data** to create a holistic **healthcare database** for **India**.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 5 hours, and another pipe can empty the same tank in 10 hours. How long will it take for both pipes to fill the tank when working together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for Filling pipe (A) = 5 hours

Time for Emptying pipe (B) = 10 hours

Net time taken = (A × B) ÷ (B − A)

Net time = (5 × 10) ÷ (10 − 5) = 50 ÷ 5 = 10 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Filling Pipe A takes 5 hours and Emptying Pipe B takes 10 hours.

Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 5 and 10.

⇒ Total Capacity = 10 units

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes
 Time (hr)
 Capacity
 Efficiency
 
 

 Pipe A (Fill)
 5
 
 10
 
 +2
 
 

 Pipe B (Empty)
 10
 −1
 
 

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B

⇒ Combined Efficiency = 2 + (−1) = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time required = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 10 ÷ 1 = 10 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Work Principle

In pipes and cisterns, work done by a filling pipe is positive, whereas work done by an emptying pipe or a leak is negative.

One-hour Work

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, the part filled in 1 hour = 1/x. If both are open, net part filled in 1 hour = 1/x − 1/y.

Inlet-Outlet condition

The tank will only fill if the efficiency of the inlet pipe is greater than the efficiency of the outlet pipe (i.e., x < y).

questions.question:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.**

Q.** Four runners – **Ravi, Sahil, Tarun, and Uday** – run at different speeds.**
Who is the fastest?****
(I)** Tarun runs faster than Ravi but slower than Sahil.**
(II)** Uday runs slower than Sahil but faster than Tarun.

options.text: Data in both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. Tarun runs faster than Ravi but slower than Sahil.

II. Uday runs slower than Sahil but faster than Tarun.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I → We get Sahil > Tarun > Ravi, but no comparison with Uday → Not sufficient.

II. From Statement II → We get Sahil > Uday > Tarun, but no comparison with Ravi → Not sufficient.

Using both I and II together →

From Statement I: Sahil > Tarun > Ravi

From Statement II: Sahil > Uday > Tarun

Combining both → Sahil > Uday > Tarun > Ravi

So, Sahil is the fastest runner.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**
